title: Im converting my project blueprints (UE4) fully to C++ so that I can work with AI. Is this a good plan? Or should I just start a new project?
author: FutureLynx_
selftext: Though its excruciatingly slow. Converting 1 class took me 1 hour.

replies.body:

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
No garbage collector, hardware/cpu cache control, directly compiles to machine code, has basically the most efficient balance of control vs organized abstraction.

There's a reason every major engine is built on it.

replies.author: vlad_h
replies.body: No. No garbage collector and you have to collect the garbage yourself. OOP is available in most modern languages. And compiles to machine code, sure, but who cares, we are no longer working with limited resources or embedded software for the space station. And just because game engines use it, still, is their problem, not a justification for modern development.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
Go build an open world game with 5 billion polys worth of landscape in the horizon, and then get back to me on how well that goes. Then build the same in Unreal.

Garbage collection, data  streaming, etc is virtually seamless in engines like Unreal assuming you're not being stupid about it, whereas have fun managing forced routines and collection strategies, as well as just horribly inefficient asset streaming to the point that you better be preloading your assets a good 20-60 seconds ahead of time or enjoy brutal freezes as the program waits for the data. I've built a game that had to load hundreds of sprites on screen simultaneously, and without setting up dedicated windows ahead of time to load the data (which is not easy when the game is procedural and RNG based, NOT a scripted, scene-based setup where you can just organize your packages chronologically) you'll experience huge hitches and freezes, even with a top of the line PC, because you are so limited by the abstracted JS language and its constraints.

Games are almost like soft realtime systems and you don't want unpredictable GC pauses in it.

replies.author: Pale-Charge-5343
replies.body:
Use C++ if you don't mind dealing with it, having full access to Gameplay Ability System alone is worth it. The hardest part is learning which class does what since Unreal uses it's own types for everything. It also handles garbage collection for you the only thing you have to really deal with is null checking. 

Also I feel like majority of the unreal engine documentation is written as comments in the c++ source files so you'll have easy access to that too, their comments are actually quite descriptive in many cases.
